topic: Git branching for payment releases
question: Jordan Voss is about to ship Harbor Bike Co’s next authorize change for fictional BayPay. How should payment-service branches, pull requests, and protected main work so Avery Chen’s POST /api/v1/payments is minted from a reviewed SHA — and what do you refuse to do when a merge goes wrong?
followUps: What belongs in a conventional review of a Terraform or pipeline PR versus a docs typo?
A teammate wants a long-lived release/east branch as the second trunk. How do you answer?
expectedConcepts: Trunk-based short-lived PRs into protected main
Required CI (./mvnw test on JDK 21) plus human review
Revert with a new commit; never force-push main
Git is the release control plane, not the secret store or Terraform state
engineerAnswer: I cut a short-lived branch, open a PR, wait for ./mvnw test on Java 21 and a review, then merge to main. Main is protected: no force-push, no unsigned hotfix. If 3.8.1 is wrong I revert with a new commit that points the task back at 3.8.0. I never commit BAYPAY_DB_* or AWS keys. BayPay is fictional; the audit still has to say which SHA minted the ECR tag.
seniorAnswer: Trunk-based: main is the only integration branch that may publish baypay/payment-service:<immutable-tag> in us-west-2. I require CI plus a conventional review that names tests, secrets, image tag, cost if apply is possible, and rollback. LGTM is not a review. GitFlow with a permanent release/east is a second trunk nobody can delete. If apply went badly, I revert HCL and the image_tag with a new commit — force-pushing main to ‘clean history’ destroys Priya Nair’s timeline. State and Secrets Manager stay out of git.
staffAnswer: I treat git as desired state for the pipeline, not as the AWS API. App repo, workflow YAML, and Terraform roots may split, but only main publishes an image or plans the prod/student backend. Blast radius of a bad merge is the next immutable tag plus whatever image_tag Terraform still declares — so rollback is revert plus health, not rewrite. I measure time-to-revert and reject admin exemptions on production protection. Leftover Liberty Ansible lives in its own path; I will not hide server.xml in an ECS module PR. Student sandboxes may loosen protection to learn the shape; I will not interview as if that is how BayPay production works.
principalAnswer: I set the org rule: payments, IAM, Terraform, and pipeline credentials need two sets of eyes; history is an audit artifact for a fictional regulated payment API. I fund branch protection that denies force-push and deletion even for admins, and I make revert-plus-validate the taught incident cleanup. Long-lived regional trunks and ‘hotfix on main from a laptop’ are process defects I will name in an exec review. I will not accept BayOps or a model dump as proven RCA for a bad merge. The narrative to finance is reconstructability: which commit charged Avery Chen, and who signed it.
commonMistakes: Force-pushing main after a bad apply so history looks clean.
Treating a long-lived release/east or develop branch as the default second trunk.
Approving your own Terraform with a one-word LGTM and no rollback sentence.
scoreRubric: Engineer: names short-lived PR, protected main, revert not force-push, no secrets in git. Senior: conventional review checklist, only main publishes, distinguishes GitFlow from trunk. Staff: blast radius of merge vs Terraform image_tag, no admin exemption, Ansible not hidden in ECS. Principal: org/audit policy, funds protection, refuses proven-AI RCA and laptop hotfixes as culture.

topic: CI that proves tests before an image exists

CI used a global mvn on JDK 17 because it was already on the image. What is wrong?
expectedConcepts: Verify (compile + test) before publish (image) before apply (Terraform)
Pinned JDK 21 and repo ./mvnw, not a random global Maven
No image publish from a red build; no secrets in workflow YAML
Unit/slice tests are not a merchant-healthy cut
engineerAnswer: Every PR runs ./mvnw -B test with Java 21 using the wrapper. If tests fail, we do not push an image and we do not merge. I print java -version in the log. I do not put BAYPAY_DB_PASSWORD or access keys in the workflow file. A green test means this SHA still compiles the reactor; it does not mean Harbor Bike Co can pay.
seniorAnswer: The locked pipeline is Git → CI test → image → Terraform → validate. Publish is L-12.3; apply is optional and not the student bar. I pin Temurin 21 and ./mvnw so laptop JDK 17 cannot mint production bytes. PR jobs verify only — they must not apply Terraform, push :latest, or publish from a red module. I still say out loud that tests are not ALB health or readiness on 8080. If someone skips tests ‘because Terraform is the real lab,’ I block the merge.
staffAnswer: I design the pipeline so main cannot move on a failing payment-service, shared, or sibling module, and so student forks never get the prod apply role. I separate verify, publish, and apply with different identities. I watch for ‘works on my machine’ when CI uses image mvn and developers use ./mvnw. I add a secrets scan, but I do not treat a scan as a substitute for review. I will fail a change that publishes then tests, or that builds the image to ‘save time’ before the reactor is green. terraform validate stays the AWS grade path; CI must not require apply to prove tests.
principalAnswer: I fund one cheap proof before we spend ECR storage or an ALB hour: the same Java 21 tests that encode idempotency and the state machine. I will not let a platform optimization (build once, test in the image) invert that gate without an explicit contract. I tell executives that a red build which still tagged 3.8.1 is a change-management failure, not a clever acceleration. I refuse auto-publish from a model-written workflow and I refuse to call a green image proven RCA that the SHA is merchant-safe. Rollback of a never-tested tag is how you burn the 99.9% budget on fiction.
commonMistakes: Publishing baypay/payment-service:latest or any tag from a red ./mvnw test.
Running CI on JDK 17/22 or a global mvn that is not the repo wrapper.
Treating a green unit suite as proof the Fargate task is Ready.
scoreRubric: Engineer: ./mvnw test on 21 before image; no secrets in YAML. Senior: verify/publish/apply split; PR cannot apply; tests ≠ readiness. Staff: identities, fork permissions, no test-after-publish, validate not apply as proof. Principal: funds the cheap gate, refuses inverted pipelines and ‘proven’ green-image RCA.

topic: Terraform state and blast radius for BayPay

followUps: What belongs in remote state versus git, and what do you do if state was already committed?
Which resources must a 90-minute lab refuse even if someone wants ‘realism’?

S3 backend plus DynamoDB lock in production; local/paper for students
terraform validate is the student AWS bar; apply is optional and destroyable
Blast radius: ALB, ECS service, IAM, leftover spend; no EKS/NAT/RDS apply
engineerAnswer: State records real ids. I do not commit *.tfstate. Production uses a remote backend with a lock; students may keep local state on paper. I run terraform validate to pass. If I cannot spend, I stop there. If I apply, I tag Course=AEJE and destroy the same day. I never put BAYPAY_DB_PASSWORD in .tfvars.
seniorAnswer: Two applies without a lock can both think they own the ALB or the ECS service and fight. Remote state plus a DynamoDB lock is how Sam Okada prevents that in production. State can contain secret attributes, so a committed tfstate is a security incident: rotate, then revert with a new commit — do not force-push main to hide it. Validate needs no creds and is the grade bar. Plan is useful with creds. Apply costs an ALB day and Fargate hours; I estimate first. I refuse EKS, NAT Gateway, and multi-AZ RDS in a student apply.
staffAnswer: I size blast radius by what one root module can destroy: the student ALB, the Fargate service, the ECR repo policy, and IAM that reads Secrets Manager. I split modules so a network change does not rewrite the task definition by accident, and I keep image_tag as a variable so a bad apply is a pin, not a rewrite of the VPC. I will not share one state file across staging and a laptop. Leftover Liberty is not in this state — Ansible must not be the second apply path for ECS. If someone ‘fixed’ drift in the console, I treat that as unreviewed desired-state drift, not as proven RCA.
principalAnswer: I fund remote state, locking, and least-privilege apply roles as the control plane for a fictional payment estate. I tell finance that validate is how we teach without a bill, and that an overnight ALB is a process failure. I will not accept console-click HA or a second-region apply as the 99.99% answer. I set policy: state is not git, apply is not the interview flex, and hiding a leaked state file with a force-push is a firing-class audit break. BayPayCell is not a Terraform backend and not a failover target.
commonMistakes: Committing terraform.tfstate or passwords in .tfvars, then force-pushing main to hide it.
Treating terraform apply as required to pass; ignoring validate.
Applying EKS, NAT, or multi-AZ RDS ‘for realism’ in a 90-minute lab.
scoreRubric: Engineer: state not in git; validate to pass; no secrets in tfvars. Senior: lock, rotate-if-leaked, validate/plan/apply cost split, refused resources. Staff: module blast radius, one-state-per-env, console drift is not RCA. Principal: funds backend/roles, validate-as-teaching-bar, no cell failover, no force-push cleanup.

topic: module boundaries vs copy-paste stacks

When is a fourth module the wrong answer compared with a variable?

Root wires outputs; image_tag is a variable, never :latest
Copy-paste stacks drift health checks and tags
Modules are not Ansible and do not recreate BayPayCell

Health stays /actuator/health/liveness and /actuator/health/readiness on 8080. I still terraform validate the root. I do not paste a second copy of the ALB listener ‘just for staging’.
seniorAnswer: Copy-paste is how one stack probes /health and another probes /ready while merchants use payments.apps.baypay.example. Modules own one concern: network does not create NAT for realism; ecr does not push bytes; ecs does not template server.xml; alb does not own the production Route 53 zone. image_tag stays a root variable so Jordan Voss can pin 3.8.0 without forking the module. I version module source. Validate remains the student bar for each root.

Network changes rarely and can take staging and student down together if they share a state — so they share a module, not a state file. ECS changes with every tag; I will not bury image_tag inside a released module version that two environments cannot pin independently. I reject a ‘platform mega-module’ that creates EKS plus RDS plus the payment task. I also reject a seventh micro-module for every security-group rule. BUILD-1202 is extract-to-share; it is not an excuse to apply a second region. Leftover cell objects do not get a terraform module that resurrects dmgr-east.
principalAnswer: I fund a small module catalog with owners: Sam Okada for network/alb contracts, Riley for ecs health and tag pin, Jordan for the image that module.ecs consumes. A mega-module that applies EKS, NAT, and RDS, or a module that recreates BayPayCell.
Hard-coding :latest or the image tag inside the ecs module so environments cannot pin independently.

Staff: shared module ≠ shared state; change-frequency boundaries; no cell module. Principal: catalog owners, drift as SLO risk, ADR against clone-a-region-as-HA.

For fictional BayPay, when do you use Ansible, when do you refuse user-data as the release, and what is already done by the image?

Where may BAYPAY_DB_* live in each model, and where must they never live?

Ansible templates leftover Liberty server.xml/env only
User-data is EC2 bootstrap, not the teaching default
IaC creates objects; config automation is not a second control plane for ECS

Ansible, if anything, copies a server.xml shape onto a leftover Liberty VM I still own — not onto Fargate, which has no SSH. I do not put passwords in playbooks or user-data. principalAnswer: I tell the exec team the leftover Liberty host is a decommission story (Module 6), not a second product. The immutable image is how we keep Jordan’s tag, Priya’s rollback, and the 99.9% budget on one object. 99.99% HA is multi-AZ tasks, not two snowflake VMs. Failover to BayPayCell is a finding. Recreating BayPayCell / dmgr-east / PaymentCluster with playbooks.
Embedding BAYPAY_DB_PASSWORD in user-data, extra-vars, or a committed server.env.

followUps: Which changes still ship during an error-budget freeze, and which wait?
Where does a BayOps suggestion sit relative to Jordan Voss’s tag and humanApproval?

Freeze features; stabilize/rollback still ships as a reviewed PR
humanApproval pending until a named human; no auto-remediate

Force-pushing main or bouncing dmgr-east as the Friday ‘gate’.
Shipping a marketing flag during a freeze, or treating apply as an unestimated default.

Raising desired count or bouncing dmgr-east to force an unhealthy revision.
Using a jump-box :8080 200 as proof merchants can complete HTTPS.

topic: rollback that is not 'redeploy the last tag and pray'
question: A bad payment-service revision is taking Harbor Bike Co creates. Design a rollback for fictional BayPay that a Staff engineer can sign — not ‘redeploy the last tag and pray,’ not a force-push, and not a leftover cell bounce.
followUps: ECS already rolled back via circuit breaker. What is still wrong if Terraform still says 3.8.1?
What do you snapshot before you hide the scene, and what stays unproven?

Git revert plus Terraform apply of the previous image_tag
Desired state must match the kept revision
No force-push, no BayPayCell, no proven-AI RCA required to stabilize
engineerAnswer: I pin the last good ECS revision or let the circuit breaker keep 3.8.0. I open a revert PR — no force-push — so image_tag matches. I watch readiness on 8080. I do not SSH to Fargate and I do not bounce dmgr-east. I do not need a finished RCA to stabilize merchants.
seniorAnswer: Rollback is two planes. Control plane: circuit breaker or update-service to the previous task definition. Desired state: a new git commit that sets image_tag back and, if we applied, terraform apply of that pin. If I only click redeploy 3.8.0 and leave HCL forward, the next apply re-breaks production. Ansible rollback is only for a leftover Liberty cut. I quote deployment events; I do not call them proven root cause. I refuse :latest because you cannot roll back a moving tag.

I snapshot task events, Ready count, and a correlationId before the scene changes. Stabilize first (fail ready, pin revision), then remediate with the revert. I measure time-to-rollback. I will fail a design that requires a human to remember the previous tag from Slack. I will not wait for an AI dump to mark RCA proven before I pin.

I tell risk we can return Avery Chen to a known SHA without rewriting history. I will not accept ‘redeploy and pray,’ force-push, or failover to BayPayCell as the DR/rollback story. 99.9% is what we spend while we pin; 99.99% is whether one bad task in one AZ can take the year — not a reason to skip the git revert. Models suggest; named humans approve the pin.

Force-pushing main or failing over to BayPayCell / dmgr-east.
Waiting for proven AI RCA before stabilizing, or bouncing Postgres with no datastore evidence.

topic: TCP vs application timeout on a payment call
question: Avery Chen’s browser sits on POST /api/v1/payments while Riley Okonkwo sees the Fargate task still Running. How do you separate a TCP timeout from an application timeout on fictional BayPay’s authorize path, and why does the layer you pick change the stabilize?
followUps: Which timeouts sit on the ALB, the JVM HTTP client, Hikari, and the servlet container?
A SYN sits unanswered. Is that the same incident class as a 30-second servlet that finally returns 201?
expectedConcepts: TCP connect/handshake vs HTTP read vs application deadline
ALB idle timeout, servlet/Tomcat, Hikari connection timeout
Late 201 can still miss the merchant authorize window
Jump-box TCP to :8080 is not the merchant HTTPS path
engineerAnswer: I ask whether we failed to connect, connected and got no HTTP, or got a slow 201. TCP problems show in ss/syn. Application timeouts are our client or servlet deadline while the socket is up. I check readiness and I do not call a late COMPLETED a success for Harbor Bike Co. I do not bounce dmgr-east because a socket timed out.
seniorAnswer: Connect timeout means the ALB or task never accepted the handshake. Idle/read timeout means bytes stopped. An application timeout is a deadline inside payment-service or its HTTP client to a processor — the TCP session may still be ESTABLISHED. Hikari connection-timeout is a pool wait, not a SYN problem. I align ALB idle, servlet, and client so we fail before the merchant retries and double-posts; Idempotency-Key is what makes the retry safe. A jump-box curl to :8080 only proves the task TCP path, not payments.apps.baypay.example.
staffAnswer: I map a timeout budget for the golden create: P99 teaching tail is 400 ms, so a 60-second ALB idle with a 2-second Hikari timeout is a lying stack. I look for CLOSE_WAIT piles versus THREADS blocked on socketRead. I will not ‘fix’ a TCP class by raising every deadline until the 99.9% budget hides a stall. I treat timeout-as-5xx as SLO burn; a correct frozen-account 4xx is not. I refuse a stabilize that fails over to BayPayCell because ‘the network is weird.’ If a model says ‘proven: database down,’ I still need a Hikari or TCP quote.
principalAnswer: I fund one timeout story across edge, JVM, and pool so on-call does not argue layers during a page. I tell the business a late authorize is a missed window even when TCP eventually delivers. I will not buy a second region to paper over a connect timeout in us-west-2 — that is HA hygiene, not DR. 99.99% architecture includes the identity and edge path; a TCP success to :8080 with a merchant TLS/read failure still spends the year. I want RCAs that name the layer, not the person who ‘set the timeout wrong.’
commonMistakes: Treating every hang as ‘the database’ or bouncing dmgr-east.
Raising all timeouts until a late 201 looks green.
Equating jump-box TCP to :8080 with a successful merchant payment call.
scoreRubric: Engineer: connect vs app deadline; late 201 not success; no cell bounce. Senior: ALB/servlet/Hikari/client alignment; idempotent retry. Staff: budget vs P99, socket vs thread evidence, timeout burns 99.9%. Principal: org timeout contract, layer-named RCA, 99.99% includes edge, no region-as-bandaid.

topic: TLS handshake failure: cert, SNI, or protocol
question: Merchants fail HTTPS to payments.apps.baypay.example while a jump box gets HTTP 200 from the task on 8080. For fictional BayPay, how do you decide whether the handshake died on the leaf certificate, SNI, or protocol version — without treating that class as a finished RCA?
followUps: What is the teaching leaf lifetime and the 30-day / 7-day expiry contract?
How is this plane different from a cluster Secret hostname problem?
expectedConcepts: Edge TLS terminates at ALB/Ingress; task stays :8080 unless mTLS
Name mismatch, SNI host, TLS version/cipher, chain trust
Merchants-fail-TLS / tasks-healthy is a symptom class
Cluster Secret TLS versus edge ACM/DNS are different planes
